title: The rate surprise
subtitle: One policy signal, several valuation channels.
summary: An unexpected policy signal can change the path investors expect for rates. Trace the valuation and funding channels separately. Bond yields, company earnings and digital-asset demand have many other drivers; this map is an investigation framework, not an attribution model.

edges.label: Expectations move first
edges.explanation: Monetary policy communication can influence expectations for short-term rates and, through them, longer-term yields.
edges.caveat: An anticipated announcement may already be priced in. Inflation expectations and term premia can move independently.

edges.label: A different discount rate
edges.explanation: Changes in the discount rate investors apply can alter the present value of expected corporate earnings.
edges.caveat: A Treasury yield is not the full equity discount rate. Risk premia and earnings expectations also matter.

edges.label: The cost of funding changes
edges.explanation: Policy affects financial conditions, including borrowing costs and the availability of credit.
edges.caveat: A particular borrower's funding depends on its credit quality, maturity and lenders, not only the policy rate.

edges.label: Future earnings, valued today
edges.explanation: Holding expected earnings constant, a higher required discount rate lowers their present value.
edges.caveat: Earnings and risk premia rarely stay constant. Good growth news can offset a higher rate.

edges.label: A risk-capacity hypothesis
edges.explanation: Tighter funding could constrain leveraged risk taking in connected digital-asset markets. Treat this as a hypothesis to investigate.
edges.caveat: This source supports leverage and liquidity channels, not a stable rate-to-Bitcoin relationship. Flows, regulation and crypto-specific events may dominate.
